$comment: Which DTCG $types can be a Figma VARIABLE, and where the rest actually live. ONE declaration, read by both the generator (validation/build-token-axes.py, which stamps every token) and the checker (validation/figma-representable.py, which verifies tokens.json on disk conforms). Two programs reading one contract, rather than two programs each holding their own copy and agreeing with themselves.

provenance.method: empirical — a real import of all 794 tokens into Figma file ip2wZ3UUQ5sbFc3r902kYK via figma-console-mcp, then reading back every created variable's resolvedType and value. Not transcribed from a documentation page.
provenance.what_it_cost: The import reported 'Created 776 variable(s). 0 failed.' 14 of those 776 were variables holding nothing — typography/scale/h1 resolved to FLOAT 0, elevation/shadow/raised to FLOAT 0, density/stage/type-scale to a comma-joined string of alias syntax. A designer opening the picker would have chosen a name that returned nothing, in a file reporting full coverage. See correction C-017.
provenance.the_part_that_worked: The 18 motion tokens were REFUSED by the Plugin API with a message naming the four creatable types. Honest absence is the correct outcome for a token with no Figma representation. The failure mode to prevent is not absence — it is silent degradation into a representable-but-meaningless type.

dimension_unit.$comment: A second, quieter failure of the same kind, found 2026-08-31 immediately after the first. Every dimension token imported as its rem NUMBER with the unit discarded — Figma FLOAT variables are unitless. typography/size/07 arrived as 3.875 and elevation/spacing/13 as 10. Bound to a font size or a padding, Figma reads a FLOAT as PIXELS, so the display level would have rendered at 3.875px instead of 62px. Nothing failed and nothing warned; the numbers were simply wrong by a factor of 16.
dimension_unit.rule: tokens.json is the source and STAYS IN REM — rem is correct for CSS and must not be changed to suit a downstream surface. Figma has no rem, so the bridge converts on the way in and only on the way in. A dimension pushed to Figma without this conversion is off by 16x.
dimension_unit.affected: spacing (13) + typography.size (7) + typography.tracking (7). elevation.shadow geometry is authored in px already and is NOT converted — converting it would introduce the same error in the opposite direction.
dimension_unit.corroboration: After conversion, size/07 reads 62px and tracking/07 reads -2px. Those are the two independently evidenced values in the type axis [ART-005 § Type; brand.md §4] — the only two points on the scale that research fixed rather than authored. Both landing exactly is the check that the factor is right.
dimension_unit.enforced_by: validation/build-figma-tokens.py — generates design-system/tokens/coforge.figma.tokens.json, the ONLY file Figma imports. The conversion happens there, so the import is correct by construction; `--check` fails CI if tokens.json moved without regenerating. This replaced a hand-applied fix that nothing could verify, because CI has no Figma access and a re-import would have reverted all 27 dimensions silently.
dimension_unit.one_import_source: design-system/tokens/ must contain exactly ONE file matching the importer's *.tokens.json glob, and it must be the generated one. A coforge.tokens.json symlink to tokens.json existed as a workaround for the glob and was deleted on 2026-08-31 — with both present, an import would have pushed the rem source alongside the px file.

representable.$comment: DTCG $type -> the Figma variable resolvedType it becomes.

elsewhere.$comment: DTCG $type -> where the token lives instead, since it cannot be a variable. A token carrying one of these MUST declare $extensions.coforge.figma_representable: false and a matching figma_home. 'figma-*' values name a real Figma primitive the token should be materialised into; 'code-only' means Figma has no representation at all and the token is consumed exclusively in code.

reasons.$comment: Why each non-representable class has no variable form. Written once here rather than repeated on every affected token.
reasons.typography: A composite of family, size, weight and tracking. Figma expresses this as a TEXT STYLE, which can itself bind each of its fields to the size/, weight/, tracking/ and family/ variables that DO import. The composite is not lost — it is materialised as the Figma primitive that actually models it.
reasons.shadow: A composite of colour, offset, blur and spread — and DTCG allows a list of layers, which is how elevation.shadow.none expresses zero shadow as []. Figma models this as an EFFECT STYLE. Imported as a variable it collapses to FLOAT 0, which is indistinguishable from a real zero.
reasons.gradient: A list of colour stops. Figma models this as a PAINT STYLE.
reasons.duration: Figma has a Timing variable type in its own UI but the Plugin API cannot create one — verified by the API's own refusal message, which lists only BOOLEAN/COLOR/FLOAT/STRING as creatable. A duration could be smuggled in as a unitless FLOAT, and must not be: 150 with the 'ms' stripped is a number that no longer says what it measures.
reasons.cubicBezier: Four control points. No Figma variable type holds an ordered tuple.
reasons.transition: A composite of a duration and an easing, so it inherits both exclusions.
reasons.border: A composite of width, style and colour.
reasons.strokeStyle: An enumerated stroke pattern with no Figma variable equivalent.
reasons.coforge.levelSet: Not a value at all — a CONSTRAINT naming which typography.scale levels a density register is permitted to draw from. cf-type-scale declares all 8 levels; stage permits 5 and document 6, so the constraint carries real information held nowhere else. But a constraint is not a thing a designer picks from a variable picker. It belongs beside the component contract's variants, and is consumed in code.
